77675e1b:  ;Evaluate validity of field data. No editing if computed multiple.
6f628945:  ;Read input data for field.
1f59404d: Quit if the input mode is not set to standard editing.
be728a66: Increment the current input line number and clear the input buffer.
27854c34: Transfer control to the line specified by the current input line number.

bab2679c: If the line being edited is a Word-Processing field, go to the PR (Prompt) label if a Data Entry instruction exists for the current line number, otherwise execute the W (Write) and TR (Terminate Read) subroutines.

2d6446b3: If no input is entered, go to the A (Accept) label unless the field is Read-only, in which case go to the X (Exit) label. If the field is a Multiple, go to the X label. If the field is Computed and the computation result is negative, go to the A label.
833a22ce: If the input is a question mark, go to the QS (Query String) label. If the input starts with an up-arrow, execute the D (Delete) subroutine and transfer control to the ^DIE17 routine.
6534e9bc: If the input is an at-sign, execute the D subroutine and transfer control to the Z^DIE2 routine.

4292d75f: If the input is a space and the field is Date/Time word-processing with a Default value stored in the DISV global for the current user and application, set the input to the Default value and write it to the terminal unless the field is Computed or Set to No Output.

dff32ccf: If the input passes the Data Type and Input Transform, transfer control to the appropriate routine based on the field type. If the field is a Multiple, go to the M^DIE17 routine. If the field is Variable, go to the ^DIE3 routine. If the field is not Set to No Output, execute the Post-Input Transform if one exists, set the external and internal values, execute any Input Code if it exists, and write the external value to the terminal unless the field is being edited as part of a word-processing field. Otherwise, go to the V (Validate) label.
80fe24c6: ;Check if the user needs to see a help message and display it if needed.
fb5d004e: ;Write the portion of the description that was not explained to the user.
8192cc5a: ;If the data value is a pointer, look up the entry in the pointed-to file.
7be99933: ;If the data value is numeric, check if it exceeds the maximum length and skip input if it does.
7188fdde: ;If the data value is numeric with a decimal point, strip trailing zeros and remove the decimal point if the fractional part is zero.
c9e89f58: Evaluate the entry in the X array and kill YS.
bd6e85b6: Kill DIC('S') and DLAYGO. If X is defined and not equal to the up-arrow character, store X in DG(DW). If DV contains 'd', store X in ^DISV(DUZ,'DIE',DLB). Go to label A.
009383df: Write a bell character and two question marks. If DB(DQ) is defined, go to label Z^DIE17.
75df8305: Set X to the string '?BAD'.
5313d5d0: Set DZ to X. Call subroutine D, then QQ^DIEQ. Go to label B.
6b8ab585: Set D to DIFLD and DQ(DQ) to DLB_U_DV_U_DU_U_DW_U_$P($T(@('X'_DQ)),' ',2,99). Quit.

942131c0: If DE(DQ) is not defined, call subroutine O and go to label RD if X does not equal '@', go to label A if DV does not contain 'R' and X equals '@', or go to label X if X equals '@'. Set X to Y and go to label N.
d56bf501: Set DG to DV, Y to DE(DQ), and X to DU. If DQ(DQ,2) is defined, execute it. Go to label RP.

f069e59b: If DG contains 'P' and the global node ^(0) exists for the global specified by X, set X to the second piece of that node. Go to label RP if the global node ^(Y,0) does not exist. Otherwise, set Y to the first piece of that node, X to the third piece of the DD(X,.01,0) node, and DG to the second piece of the ^(0) node. Go to label R.

f07bdb6f: If DG contains 'V', Y is a number, the second piece of Y delimited by ';' contains '(', and the global node specified by the second piece exists, set X to the second piece of that node. Go to label RP if the global node ^(+Y,0) does not exist. Otherwise, set Y to the first piece of that node. If DD(+X,.01,0) exists, set DG to the second piece of that node and X to the third piece of that node. Go to label R.
5a6c8faa: Retrieve the default value for a field from the Special Syntax field in the DD (Data Dictionary).
560da793: If the user does not enter a value, set X to the default edit value (DE(DQ)). If DV is null (no input transform), the user cannot edit (DC<2), or the user deleted the value (DC<1), quit.
c314035d: If the input transform does not contain an "I" (internal) or "#" (number) code, branch to the reader.
f1d16f7c: Execute the input transform (E^DIE0). If X was set by the transform, branch to the reader. Otherwise, go to prompt mode.
7cced0fd: Quit the input template (no further processing).
a30bfa90: Initialize variables used by the input template.
780cd545: Set field properties for the DATE SIGNED field (#10.05).
a88fe71e: Quit if RE is true.
eef01f63: Get current date and time in external format. Set X to the date/time value or kill X if it's less than 1.
e6d44edf: Quit.

5427ea7d: If DG is defined and has more than 9 nodes, call FileMan's EN^DIE17 to edit file entry. Set Y to up-arrow, DQ to 2, call X2, and either quit or continue based on value of Y. If Y is defined and not up-arrow, set X to Y, set DIC(0) to 'F' for FileMan lookup, set DW to DQ, and transfer control to OUT^DIE17.
